Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

Healthwatch is your health and social care champion. If you use GPs and hospitals, dentists, pharmacies, care homes or other support services, we want to hear about your experiences.

As an independent statutory body, we have the power to make sure NHS leaders and other decision makers listen to your feedback and improve standards of care.

We can also help you to reliable and trustworthy information and advice. Last year, we helped nearly a million people like you to have your say and get the support you need.

Wherever you live in England, you will have a local Healthwatch nearby (there are over 150 across the country). We are here to listen to the issues that really matter to local communities and to hear about your experiences of using health and social care services.

We are entirely independent and impartial, and any information you share with us is confidential. Healthwatch uses your feedback to better understand the challenges facing the NHS and other care providers nationally, to make sure your experiences improve health and care services for everyone.

We can also help you to get the information and advice you need to make the right decisions for you and to get the support you deserve.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

NHS Cardiovascular Disease (CVD) Health Checks – Outreach
 
A free NHS Health Check is a quick and simple way to check your overall health and help you take action to reduce your risk of developing serious conditions such as heart disease stroke diabetes kidney disease and dementia.
 
Our practitioners will measure your blood pressure take your height and weight measurements check your cholesterol and blood glucose levels. They will also discuss your lifestyle. From these checks you will be given a risk score and that indicates the likelihood of having a cardiovascular event in the next 10 years.  They will help you understand your results and what they mean and provide advice and support on staying healthy. The practitioner will also refer or signpost you to other services if needed.
 
The whole appointment takes 30 minutes so if you are aged 40-74 a resident in Somerset AND / OR registered with a Somerset GP have not had an NHS Health Check already in the past 5 years and have no pre-existing conditions or on certain types of medication you are eligible for a health check!
 
The health checks are currently taking place across Somerset in Wells Yeovil Chard Glastonbury Taunton Langport libraries and at the SHAPE Mendip Council Offices. Details of locations and booking links can be found here: Health Check locations . There will be other locations added in the future.
 
You can book online to ensure your check is booked or you can drop in.

ElementText:
Eclypse is a free and confidential service for young people aged 25 and under in Manchester. We provide support for anyone who is concerned about their own or somebody else’s drug or alcohol use. Our friendly team is on hand to provide advice and tailored support plans to help you achieve your goals. We’re a confidential service, which means we won’t inform anyone of your involvement with us, unless there was a risk of harm to yourself or somebody else. We work in a way that suits you – that might be having appointments over the phone, in-person at our base or your place of choosing, or online via Zoom. 

Eclypse provide access to treatment (drugs/alcohol) and offer holistic support to children, young people and families.  Support can include vaping cessation, sexual health advice, education and training, and employment for 18-24 year olds, stress and anxiety management, improving self-esteem and lots more. Our Family Team work with children affected by parental/family substance misuse to promote resilience and family unity. We can also signpost support for people concerned about a young person’s drug/alcohol use, as we understand the difficulties this can bring to people of any age.

Eclypse will work with any young person living in the Manchester City Council borough, or going to school in the Manchester borough if they want to have appointments at school. There are similar services on offer in neighbouring areas of Salford, Trafford, Rochdale, Oldham and other Greater Manchester areas.

Eclypse also offer groupwork programmes and can deliver bespoke professional training. See our Eventbrite page for online training sessions we have coming up, which cover varied topics related to drugs, alcohol and young people in Manchester, aimed at professionals working within relevant areas.
Monday to Friday 9am - 5pm
Manchester

Accessing Eclypse’s support and advice is easy, and we accept both self and professional referrals. You can call or email using the contact details above, or fill in our short online referral form here - https://www.changegrowlive.org/manchester/referrals. We aim to get back to you within 48 hours.
Make sure to follow us on our socials! We’re @eclypsemanchester on Instagram and @ManchesterEclypse on Facebook!

Free and confidential advice and information for people in Herefordshire, including young people (11-17), young adults (18-24) and adults (25+), families and carers, and veterans. We have hubs in Hereford, Leominster and Ross-on-Wye, with satellites in Ledbury, Kington and Bromyard. We also provide outreach support via our recovery vehicle (Lance).

We offer a range of treatment options, including Motivational Interviewing (MI), Motivational Enhancement Therapy (MET), pathways for non-dependent and dependent alcohol users, non-opiate users, and opiate users (including Opiate Substitute Treatment, OST), and evidence-based psychosocial programmes (in person and online). We also offer harm reduction advice, needle syringe provision (NSP), and overdose awareness including naloxone/nyxoid (opiate overdose reversal drug). We offer assessments within 5 working days, with access to Introduction to Treatment (ITT) sessions to support engagement and referrals to other support services, including Individual Placement Support (IPS) to access employment. We work with service users to design a personalised care plan to meet their needs and promote service user involvement, with peer mentors and lived-experience workers to support recovery check-ins and aftercare.

Eclypse is a free and confidential service for young people aged 25 and under in Manchester. We provide support for anyone who is concerned about their own or somebody else’s drug or alcohol use. Our friendly team is on hand to provide advice and tailored support plans to help you achieve your goals. We’re a confidential service, which means we won’t inform anyone of your involvement with us, unless there was a risk of harm to yourself or somebody else. We work in a way that suits you – that might be having appointments over the phone, in-person at our base or your place of choosing, or online via Zoom. 

Eclypse provide access to treatment (drugs/alcohol) and offer holistic support to children, young people and families.  Support can include vaping cessation, sexual health advice, education and training, and employment for 18-24 year olds, stress and anxiety management, improving self-esteem and lots more. Our Family Team work with children affected by parental/family substance misuse to promote resilience and family unity. We can also signpost support for people concerned about a young person’s drug/alcohol use, as we understand the difficulties this can bring to people of any age.

Eclypse will work with any young person living in the Manchester City Council borough, or going to school in the Manchester borough if they want to have appointments at school. There are similar services on offer in neighbouring areas of Salford, Trafford, Rochdale, Oldham and other Greater Manchester areas.

Eclypse also offer groupwork programmes and can deliver bespoke professional training. See our Eventbrite page for online training sessions we have coming up, which cover varied topics related to drugs, alcohol and young people in Manchester, aimed at professionals working within relevant areas.
Monday to Friday 9am - 5pm
Manchester

The Institute of Podiatrists is a professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries diseases and traumas of the foot and lower limb. Podiatrists also prevent, manage and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC), and work in the NHS and independent/private sectors. 

Independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.

The Institute supports podiatrists throughout their career, to deliver high quality foot and lower limb care and to continue to develop their skills.

Our Stop Smoking Advisors at Healthy Hounslow have a wealth of training and experience in smoking cessation and helping clients with behaviour change. 

You can join our stop smoking programme if...
You have used tobacco/smoked in the past 48 hours, are over 12 years of age and are either:
•	A resident of Hounslow
•	A student in Hounslow
•	Working in Hounslow
•	Registered with a GP in Hounslow

You will begin with a free tailored programme which includes regular sessions with your Stop Smoking Advisor, Carbon Monoxide monitoring and access to a variety of treatments. Advisors offer a combination of face to face and telephone/online support.

We can help you find what works best for you. That might be a direct supply of Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT) or prescription medication (if applicable). Healthy Hounslow are here to support you to stay smoke-free.

You can self-refer to the service on the Healthy Hounslow website: https://healthyhounslow.co.uk/.
Available to anyone who lives, works, studies or has a GP in Hounslow

Healthwatch is your health and social care champion. If you use GPs and hospitals, dentists, pharmacies, care homes or other support services, we want to hear about your experiences.

As an independent statutory body, we have the power to make sure NHS leaders and other decision makers listen to your feedback and improve standards of care.

We can also help you to reliable and trustworthy information and advice. Last year, we helped nearly a million people like you to have your say and get the support you need.

Wherever you live in England, you will have a local Healthwatch nearby (there are over 150 across the country). We are here to listen to the issues that really matter to local communities and to hear about your experiences of using health and social care services.

We are entirely independent and impartial, and any information you share with us is confidential. Healthwatch uses your feedback to better understand the challenges facing the NHS and other care providers nationally, to make sure your experiences improve health and care services for everyone.

We can also help you to get the information and advice you need to make the right decisions for you and to get the support you deserve.

We provide individual and tailored support to meet your needs.

Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active.

While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

ElementText: Age UK Norfolk is an independent local charity dedicated to supporting older people across Norfolk to enjoy later life. We provide free, confidential information and advice on issues such as benefits, care, housing, wellbeing, and household finances, helping older people make informed choices and manage their money with confidence. Our services include a countywide advice line, face-to-face support, advocacy, help with budgeting and benefits, a range of companionship services to reduce loneliness, digital inclusion sessions, and community outreach activities.

Our Head Office is accessible my appointment only

Age UK Norfolk offers free, confidential information and advice on a wide range of issues including benefits, care options, housing, and wellbeing. Our trained advisers help older people maximise their income through benefit checks and provide step-by-step support with applications and budgeting.  We also deliver an independent advocacy service, offering one-to-one support to help people have their voices heard, make informed decisions, and manage practical matters such as household finances and bills.  To reduce loneliness and isolation, we provide a range of companionship services, including telephone befriending, face-to-face visits, and travelling companionship. In addition, we run digital inclusion sessions to help people build confidence with technology and stay connected, and we engage with communities through local events and outreach.
Contact the Advice team on 0300 500 1217 / advice@ageuknorfolk.org.uk or visit our website for information about referrals to our services.

The Greenhouse centre provides free health care services and housing and welfare advice for homeless people in Hackney. The service is for men and women who are sleeping rough, have a drug or alcohol problem, poor mental health, or who are simply struggling to keep a roof over their head. The welcoming centre provides a way to engage with these socially-excluded individuals, who can drop in informally. 

The services provided at the Greenhouse include:
- full health assessments 
- GP registration 
- TB screening 
- a needle collection service 
- housing advice 
- welfare and benefits support 
- specific advice for EU nationals, including translation services 
- specialist debt advice 
- legal advice 
- links to other support service
Please call to arrange an appointment

We’re the carers, researchers, healthcare professionals, friends, parents, runners and fundraisers all united in our ambition to ensure that one day, no one will have to live with the pain, fatigue and isolation that arthritis causes.

•Educating and informing the general public, patients and health professionals on all aspects of arthritis

If you are pregnant and would like to quit, you can access the service yourself or ask your midwife to refer you.  

Living Well Smokefree offers personalised, one-to-one support over six to 12 weeks. For as little as 30p a day* you can get:
- access to a dedicated Stop Smoking Consultant,
- a supply of either Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT),  or
- local weekly one-to-one sessions.

* Based on one quit product per person who pays prescription charges. The products are free to people who do not pay prescription charges.
Covers the whole of North Yorkshire postcodes, except York itself.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

Healthwatch is your health and social care champion. If you use GPs and hospitals, dentists, pharmacies, care homes or other support services, we want to hear about your experiences.

The Institute of Podiatrists is a professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries diseases and traumas of the foot and lower limb. Podiatrists also prevent, manage and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC), and work in the NHS and independent/private sectors. 

Independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.

The Institute supports podiatrists throughout their career, to deliver high quality foot and lower limb care and to continue to develop their skills.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

Healthwatch is your health and social care champion. If you use GPs and hospitals, dentists, pharmacies, care homes or other support services, we want to hear about your experiences.

As an independent statutory body, we have the power to make sure NHS leaders and other decision makers listen to your feedback and improve standards of care.

We can also help you to reliable and trustworthy information and advice. Last year, we helped nearly a million people like you to have your say and get the support you need.

Wherever you live in England, you will have a local Healthwatch nearby (there are over 150 across the country). We are here to listen to the issues that really matter to local communities and to hear about your experiences of using health and social care services.

We are entirely independent and impartial, and any information you share with us is confidential. Healthwatch uses your feedback to better understand the challenges facing the NHS and other care providers nationally, to make sure your experiences improve health and care services for everyone.

We can also help you to get the information and advice you need to make the right decisions for you and to get the support you deserve.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education and raising awareness of foot health. Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing and treating conditions, injuries diseases and traumas of the foot and lower limb. Podiatrists also prevent, manage and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection and keep people of all ages mobile and active. Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists), are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC), and work in the NHS and independent/private sectors. The College supports podiatrists throughout their career to deliver high quality foot and lower limb care and to continue to develop their skills.

ElementText:
The Young Person’s Drug and Alcohol Service is commissioned to provide treatment for substance misuse to young people under the age of 18, as well as those in the transitional age group of 18–29, who are affected by drug or alcohol use.
 
Services provided
·	Screening, Identification and Brief interventions
·	Comprehensive Substance Use Assessment followed by Recovery Care Plan
·	Psychosocial interventions including Motivational Interviewing, Cognitive Behavioural Informed Therapy and Relapse Prevention
·	Group Intervention Programmes
·	Recovery Group Support
·	Counselling
·	Acupuncture
·	Support accessing stop smoking service
 
The service also provides:
·	School-based universal drug and alcohol awareness and targeted group interventions
·	Support for hidden harm, those impacted by parental substance use
·	Family support for those impacted by a loved ones substance misuse

Services include:  
• Sexually Transmitted Infection (STI) testing and treatment
• Contraception,  (including injection, implant and coils) 
• Emergency contraception 
• Pregnancy testing 
• HIV testing, treatment and care
• Psychosexual counselling (by GP referral only)

Podiatrists also prevent, manage and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection and keep people of all ages mobile and active. Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists), are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC), and work in the NHS and independent/private sectors. Services include:

• Condoms and lubricant

• Emergency contraception 
• Pregnancy testing 
• Abortion referrals 
• Sexual health advice 
• PrEP 
• Vaccinations and referrals 
• Sexual assault help and support

This is an all-age service. There is no minimum age to use this service.

Living Well Smokefree has a team of advisors who have plenty of experience in helping people to stop smoking for good. They will see anyone from the age of 12, have community based locations across North Yorkshire and can arrange home visits for people who have mobility issues.
If you are pregnant and would like to quit, you can access the service yourself or ask your midwife to refer you.  

Living Well Smokefree offers personalised, one-to-one support over six to 12 weeks. For as little as 30p a day* you can get:
- access to a dedicated Stop Smoking Consultant,
- a supply of either Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT),  or
- local weekly one-to-one sessions.

* Based on one quit product per person who pays prescription charges. The products are free to people who do not pay prescription charges.
Covers the whole of North Yorkshire postcodes, except York itself.

The Institute of Chiropodists and Podiatrists is a professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries diseases and traumas of the foot and lower limb. Podiatrists also prevent, manage and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC), and work in the NHS and independent/private sectors. 

The Institute supports podiatrists throughout their career, to deliver high quality foot and lower limb care and to continue to develop their skills.

The Macular Society is a patient charity especially for people with macular conditions. We have a large network of support groups around the country where members with central vision loss can share experiences and offer one another encouragement and friendship. They are the experts on living with macular disease! Our services include • Advice and Information Service • Confidential telephone counselling (BACP accredited) • Befriending • Advocacy • Coaching in new ways of seeing • Buddy schemes for people experiencing visual hallucinations (Charles Bonnet Syndrome) and for those concerned about having injections in the eye. We offer information and support to improve lives today and we fund medical research to bring hope for the future. We have a large network of support groups around the country where members with central vision loss can share experiences and offer one another encouragement and friendship. They are the experts on living with macular disease! Our services include • Advice and Information Service • Confidential telephone counselling (BACP accredited) • Befriending • Advocacy • Coaching in new ways of seeing • Buddy schemes for people experiencing visual hallucinations (Charles Bonnet Syndrome) and for those concerned about having injections in the eye. Worried about your own or someone else’s alcohol or drug use? We offer free and confidential advice, support and treatment for people in Gloucestershire aged 18+.

We’ll talk about your concerns and make a plan together. This care plan will help you reduce or stop your drug or alcohol use – making sure you receive the right support at the right time for you. Help and advice for family, friends and carers on how best to support you during your recovery is also available.

At our service, you can get:

- Advice about your health and wellbeing
- Regular sessions with your personal keyworker
- A range of different support groups
- Women-only support and safe spaces in partnership with The Nelson Trust.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education and raising awareness of foot health. Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing and treating conditions, injuries diseases and traumas of the foot and lower limb. Podiatrists also prevent, manage and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection and keep people of all ages mobile and active. Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists), are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC), and work in the NHS and independent/private sectors. The College supports podiatrists throughout their career to deliver high quality foot and lower limb care and to continue to develop their skills.

Living Well Smokefree has a team of advisors who have plenty of experience in helping people to stop smoking for good. They will see anyone from the age of 12, have community based locations across North Yorkshire and can arrange home visits for people who have mobility issues.
If you are pregnant and would like to quit, you can access the service yourself or ask your midwife to refer you.  

Living Well Smokefree offers personalised, one-to-one support over six to 12 weeks. For as little as 30p a day* you can get:
- access to a dedicated Stop Smoking Consultant,
- a supply of either Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT),  or
- local weekly one-to-one sessions.

* Based on one quit product per person who pays prescription charges. The products are free to people who do not pay prescription charges.
Covers the whole of North Yorkshire postcodes, except York itself.

Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing and treating conditions, injuries diseases and traumas of the foot and lower limb. Podiatrists also prevent, manage and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection and keep people of all ages mobile and active. Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists), are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC), and work in the NHS and independent/private sectors. Change Grow Live Birmingham is a free and confidential drug and alcohol service for adults. We offer treatment and recovery services to support anyone experiencing difficulties with substance misuse in a range of local community and clinical settings. Our recovery teams include doctors, non-medical prescribers, recovery coordinators, nurses, recovery motivators, service user representatives, and volunteers. We also work with Intuitive Thinking Skills, DATUS, and KIKIT to provide specialist support in our Throughcare offer.

We provide:
·	Confidential advice and information about drugs and alcohol
·	A tailored package of care
·	Healthcare clinics and blood-borne virus testing
·	Residential detoxification and rehabilitation options
·	Ambulatory detox in our hubs
·	Throughcare (group sessions from our recovery motivators and partners)
·	Harm minimisation
·	Needle Exchange and safe storage
·	Shared Care (121 sessions in your local GP surgery)

Depending on your situation, you may be referred to one of our in-house specialist teams. These teams include the Women’s and Families team, Criminal Justice, IPS Employment team, the Veteran’s group, Buvidal team and Homeless & Rough Sleeper team.

We are a user led abstinence based group, which means we agree collectively to reduce, but ultimately stop the use of cannabis, spice and legal highs within our membership.
 
We recognise the damage our drug misuse can do to ourselves and those around us and we choose to seek help from others who have recovered successfully from serious addictions. We have no affiliation to other mutual aid groups such as NA (Narcotics Anonymous) and SMART (Self Management and Recovery Training) but we do support and commend their work. We often refer our members to both meetings and others. We strongly believe that no one system works for everyone and we encourage our members to experience and embrace many different recovery systems, activities and communities.

We are not a cannabis appreciation society and we do not advocate legalisation. We do however acknowledge the particular CBD health benefits and call for greater and more transparent research. Similarly we recognise the failure of subsequent governments to sufficiently support appropriate treatment and recovery programmes.

We have achieved many levels of success within our membership, our groups have produced and maintained many years of clean-time. We have done this by creating a series of local meetings in a safe, confidential, non-judgmental and supportive environment, where members can rebuild their lives together.
Website is available 24/7. Call or text for details of group times.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

Living Well Smokefree has a team of advisors who have plenty of experience in helping people to stop smoking for good. They will see anyone from the age of 12, have community based locations across North Yorkshire and can arrange home visits for people who have mobility issues.
If you are pregnant and would like to quit, you can access the service yourself or ask your midwife to refer you.  

Living Well Smokefree offers personalised, one-to-one support over six to 12 weeks. For as little as 30p a day* you can get:
- access to a dedicated Stop Smoking Consultant,
- a supply of either Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT),  or
- local weekly one-to-one sessions.

* Based on one quit product per person who pays prescription charges. The products are free to people who do not pay prescription charges.
Covers the whole of North Yorkshire postcodes, except York itself.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education and raising awareness of foot health. Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing and treating conditions, injuries diseases and traumas of the foot and lower limb. Podiatrists also prevent, manage and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection and keep people of all ages mobile and active. Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists), are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC), and work in the NHS and independent/private sectors. The College supports podiatrists throughout their career to deliver high quality foot and lower limb care and to continue to develop their skills.

- local weekly one-to-one sessions.

* Based on one quit product per person who pays prescription charges. The products are free to people who do not pay prescription charges.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education and raising awareness of foot health. Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing and treating conditions, injuries diseases and traumas of the foot and lower limb. Podiatrists also prevent, manage and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection and keep people of all ages mobile and active. Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists), are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC), and work in the NHS and independent/private sectors. The College supports podiatrists throughout their career to deliver high quality foot and lower limb care and to continue to develop their skills.

- young people

- referral to other services, with the young person's permission. PLEASE NOTE: the young person must consent to any referral that is made.
- support to reduce use of substances/stop using substances
- multi-agency partnerships
- factual, unbiased information for young people about their substance use.

We will act with the best interests of the young person in mind.

The Institute of Podiatrists is a professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries diseases and traumas of the foot and lower limb. Podiatrists also prevent, manage and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC), and work in the NHS and independent/private sectors. 

Independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.

The Institute supports podiatrists throughout their career, to deliver high quality foot and lower limb care and to continue to develop their skills.

OrganisationName: Sorted - Northumberland Young People'S Drug And Alcohol Service
ElementText:
The service provides intervention for children and young people up to age 18 within the Northumberland area. Young people are supported to stop using substances, and to reduce the associated risks from substance misuse, both to themselves and their communities. They are also supported to achieve good physical and emotional health and wellbeing. 

Sorted can help:
- young people
- professionals and agencies working with young people

Young people up to 18 years old can access the service. We offer:
- 1-2-1 indivdual support
- strict confidentiality, whilst adhering to safegaurding requirements
- referral to other services, with the young person's permission. PLEASE NOTE: the young person must consent to any referral that is made.
- support to reduce use of substances/stop using substances
- multi-agency partnerships
- factual, unbiased information for young people about their substance use.

We will act with the best interests of the young person in mind.

• A&E link work
• A 24/7 emergency referral and crisis line for young people
• Specialist prescribing and pharmacological support for prescribing needs

• Access to prescribing and needle exchange services
• Alternative therapies, such as acupuncture
• Access to mentors, aftercare and recovery support
• Transitional support to adult services
• Additional support for care leavers and those with learning difficulties/disabilities up to age 25
• Volunteering opportunities

ElementText: The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education and raising awareness of foot health. Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing and treating conditions, injuries diseases and traumas of the foot and lower limb. Podiatrists also prevent, manage and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection and keep people of all ages mobile and active. Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists), are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC), and work in the NHS and independent/private sectors. The College supports podiatrists throughout their career to deliver high quality foot and lower limb care and to continue to develop their skills.

ElementText:
Catch22 Surrey Young People’s Substance Use Service (SYPSUS) is a county-wide specialist treatment service for young people aged up to 25. We offer free and confidential advice and support.

A multi-professional team of specialist workers providing a range of support including:
• Whole-family work
• A&E link work
• A 24/7 emergency referral and crisis line for young people
• Specialist prescribing and pharmacological support for prescribing needs
• Harm-reduction approach
• Individually tailored help, based on an assessment of each young person’s needs
• Specialist support for mental health problems
• Access to prescribing and needle exchange services
• Alternative therapies, such as acupuncture
• Access to mentors, aftercare and recovery support
• Transitional support to adult services
• Additional support for care leavers and those with learning difficulties/disabilities up to age 25
• Volunteering opportunities

WithYou provide free and confidential support to people experiencing drugs, alcohol or mental health challenges. 

Get in touch with our free, confidential service and talk to one of our trained staff. We’re here to listen – you can tell us as little or as much as you want.

We’ll work with you on your own goals, whether that’s cutting down your drug or alcohol use, stopping completely or just getting a bit of advice. 

We can also support you if you’re worried about someone else’s drinking or drug use.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

The NHS Health Check Service is available at GP Practices across the Wolverhampton catchment area

If you are 40-74 years old without a pre-existing condition and are registered with a GP you should receive a letter or text inviting you for a free NHS Health Check every 5 years. Once you get your invitation follow the instructions to book your appointment. You can also ask your GP surgery to see if you are eligible.

The NHS Health Check is a simple check of your heart health. Aimed at adults in England aged 40 to 74, it checks your vascular or circulatory health and works out your risk of developing some of the most disabling – but preventable – illnesses. It is free of charge, including any follow-up tests or appointments.
Residents should contact their GP directly for an NHS Health Check

Visit GOV.UK to find your local authority.
You are only entitled to an NHS Health Check from the local authority in which you live.

ElementText:
The SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist Service offers teaching group sessions in the community, home teaching visits and parent training courses for young children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) aged 0-3 years; who are delayed in at least two areas of development

We support children and families in Southampton who meet the following eligibility criteria:
·  The family live in the Southampton local authority area, 
·  The child is aged 0-3 years, 
·  The child’s development is delayed by at least six months in two or more areas of development, 
·  Parental consent has been obtained, 
·  The child’s parent/carer must be available to meet the SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist on a regular basis, 
· Note: If a child attends an early years setting for more than 15 hours a week, this may affect the type of support that the SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist is able to offer.

SEND & Portage Early Years Stay and Play session: 
Upon receipt of a referral a Senior SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist will contact the family to arrange an initial home visit.

If the service is felt to be appropriate then this information will be communicated to the family during the initial home visit and followed up with a letter to the referrer.

SEND & Portage Early Years specialist teaching sessions: 
The main focus of the groups will be communication, requesting, making choices, shared attention and turn taking. The group will follow the same routine each week which will include:
·  Arrival activity, 
·  Welcome song & Makaton sign, 
·  Attention activity, 
·  Modelling and practicing focus of the week, 
·  Messy play/free play, 
·  Singing, 
·  Questions, 
·  These groups are an opportunity for parents to be actively involved in their child’s play and to practice new strategies alongside the SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist.

SEND & Portage Early Years home teaching sessions: 
Families receive a weekly home teaching session from their Portage teacher, usually 6-8 visits.

This may include: 
·  Assessment of the child’s strengths and the areas that they find difficult, 
·  Learning through play in partnership with a parent/carer, 
·  Advice on pre-schools/early years settings and on the support that the child may need when they start at a setting, 
·  Signposting to other services.

ElementText: What training do we have?  All SEND & Portage Early Years Specialists have:·  Foundation degree level qualifications in child development, ·  Significant experience of working within Early Years, ·  Significant experience of Special Educational Needs, ·  Significant experience of working with families, ·  Completed Portage Workshop, ·  Staff receive on-going training through the National Portage Development training program, as well as through Southampton City Council’s workforce development programme.  When necessary, we seek and provide additional training based on needs identified by the SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist, relating to working with children with specific special educational needs and disabilities.  How do we communicate with service users and how are they involved in decision?  Parents/carers and children are partners in all aspects of the SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist Service delivery.  All sessions in the home or at group includes both adult and child-led activities so that parents/carers and children have the opportunity to lead and influence the play and learning that takes place.  SEND & Portage Early Years Specialist Service will take into consideration the child’s likes and dislikes, the family’s day-to-day lives and their aspirations for their child, these are all included in the planning of each play session.  If the service is working with a family where by English is not their first language, they may ask if there’s a family member or friend who could act as a translator. If there isn’t anyone or the family don’t feel comfortable with this, employing a translator would be considered.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

If you are 40-74 years old without a pre-existing condition and are registered with a GP you should receive a letter or text inviting you for a free NHS Health Check every 5 years. Once you get your invitation follow the instructions to book your appointment. You can also ask your GP surgery to see if you are eligible.

The NHS Health Check is a simple check of your heart health. Aimed at adults in England aged 40 to 74, it checks your vascular or circulatory health and works out your risk of developing some of the most disabling – but preventable – illnesses. It is free of charge, including any follow-up tests or appointments.
Residents should contact their GP directly for an NHS Health Check

Healthwatch is your health and social care champion. If you use GPs and hospitals, dentists, pharmacies, care homes or other support services, we want to hear about your experiences.

As an independent statutory body, we have the power to make sure NHS leaders and other decision makers listen to your feedback and improve standards of care.

We can also help you to reliable and trustworthy information and advice. Last year, we helped nearly a million people like you to have your say and get the support you need.

Wherever you live in England, you will have a local Healthwatch nearby (there are over 150 across the country). We are here to listen to the issues that really matter to local communities and to hear about your experiences of using health and social care services.

We are entirely independent and impartial, and any information you share with us is confidential. Healthwatch uses your feedback to better understand the challenges facing the NHS and other care providers nationally, to make sure your experiences improve health and care services for everyone.

We can also help you to get the information and advice you need to make the right decisions for you and to get the support you deserve.

ElementText:
Change Grow Live Birmingham is a free and confidential drug and alcohol service for adults. We offer treatment and recovery services to support anyone experiencing difficulties with substance misuse in a range of local community and clinical settings. Our recovery teams include doctors, non-medical prescribers, recovery coordinators, nurses, recovery motivators, service user representatives, and volunteers. We also work with Intuitive Thinking Skills, DATUS, and KIKIT to provide specialist support in our Throughcare offer.

We provide:
·	Confidential advice and information about drugs and alcohol
·	A tailored package of care
·	Healthcare clinics and blood-borne virus testing
·	Residential detoxification and rehabilitation options
·	Ambulatory detox in our hubs
·	Throughcare (group sessions from our recovery motivators and partners)
·	Harm minimisation
·	Needle Exchange and safe storage
·	Shared Care (121 sessions in your local GP surgery)

Depending on your situation, you may be referred to one of our in-house specialist teams. These teams include the Women’s and Families team, Criminal Justice, IPS Employment team, the Veteran’s group, Buvidal team and Homeless & Rough Sleeper team.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.
This is a visiting/mobile service

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

Worried about your own or someone else’s alcohol or drug use? We offer free and confidential advice, support and treatment for people in Gloucestershire aged 18+.

We’ll talk about your concerns and make a plan together. This care plan will help you reduce or stop your drug or alcohol use – making sure you receive the right support at the right time for you. Help and advice for family, friends and carers on how best to support you during your recovery is also available.

At our service, you can get:

- Advice about your health and wellbeing
- Regular sessions with your personal keyworker
- A range of different support groups
- Women-only support and safe spaces in partnership with The Nelson Trust.
Gloucestershire

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

Beyond Dementia is a registered charity founded in 1990, in response to a locally identified need for support for people living with dementia and their Carers. The aim of Beyond Dementia is to provide a range of flexible services to support people with Alzheimer’s Disease and other dementias, and their Carers.

Beyond Dementia works closely with the Avon  & Wiltshire Mental Health Care NHS Trust, Department of Adult and Community Services and Primary Care Trusts. We are now registered and inspected as a Domiciliary Care Service Provider and also run day clubs and a wide range of community activity groups, including singing, art, exercise, and outdoor nature groups.  Our dementia advisers provide information, advice and support from point of diagnosis and stay in touch with families so they have a named contact for ongoing support. Beyond Dementia is the main specialist provider of care for people with mild to moderate dementia in Wiltshire, assisting them to maintain as much independence and control over their lives as possible.

We work alongside Carers throughout the course of the illness by providing information and emotional support. Services for family carers include peer support groups and training courses.  We reflect client individuality by responding with flexible services inside and outside the home, 7 days a week.

Worried about your own or someone else’s alcohol or drug use? We offer free and confidential advice, support and treatment for people in Gloucestershire aged 18+.

We’ll talk about your concerns and make a plan together. This care plan will help you reduce or stop your drug or alcohol use – making sure you receive the right support at the right time for you. Help and advice for family, friends and carers on how best to support you during your recovery is also available.

At our service, you can get:

- Advice about your health and wellbeing
- Regular sessions with your personal keyworker
- A range of different support groups
- Women-only support and safe spaces in partnership with The Nelson Trust.
Gloucestershire
You can visit our service in person or contact us by phone or email. Any professional, such as a housing support worker, social worker, GP or nurse can also make a referral for you.

WithYou provide free and confidential support to people experiencing drugs, alcohol or mental health challenges. 

Get in touch with our free, confidential service and talk to one of our trained staff. We’re here to listen – you can tell us as little or as much as you want.

We’ll work with you on your own goals, whether that’s cutting down your drug or alcohol use, stopping completely or just getting a bit of advice. 

We can also support you if you’re worried about someone else’s drinking or drug use.

The service provides intervention for children and young people up to age 18 within the Northumberland area. Young people are supported to stop using substances, and to reduce the associated risks from substance misuse, both to themselves and their communities. They are also supported to achieve good physical and emotional health and wellbeing. 

Sorted can help:
- young people
- professionals and agencies working with young people

Young people up to 18 years old can access the service. We offer:
- 1-2-1 indivdual support
- strict confidentiality, whilst adhering to safegaurding requirements
- referral to other services, with the young person's permission. PLEASE NOTE: the young person must consent to any referral that is made.
- support to reduce use of substances/stop using substances
- multi-agency partnerships
- factual, unbiased information for young people about their substance use.

We will act with the best interests of the young person in mind.

Healthwatch is your health and social care champion. If you use GPs and hospitals, dentists, pharmacies, care homes or other support services, we want to hear about your experiences.

As an independent statutory body, we have the power to make sure NHS leaders and other decision makers listen to your feedback and improve standards of care.

We can also help you to reliable and trustworthy information and advice. Last year, we helped nearly a million people like you to have your say and get the support you need.

Wherever you live in England, you will have a local Healthwatch nearby (there are over 150 across the country). We are here to listen to the issues that really matter to local communities and to hear about your experiences of using health and social care services.

We are entirely independent and impartial, and any information you share with us is confidential. Healthwatch uses your feedback to better understand the challenges facing the NHS and other care providers nationally, to make sure your experiences improve health and care services for everyone.

We can also help you to get the information and advice you need to make the right decisions for you and to get the support you deserve.

Lincolnshire Recovery Partnership is a free and confidential service for people in Lincolnshire who want support with their drug and alcohol use.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

ElementText:
Southend Treatment and Recovery Service (also known as STARS) is delivered by The Forward Trust alongside partners Open Road. The service helps people aged 18 or over who are experiencing challenges with their use of drugs and/or alcohol or people who are impacted indirectly because a significant other is experiencing these challenges (it doesn’t matter if the significant other is not ready to get support themselves).

Services delivered at our Southend hub include:
·  One-to-one and group support.
·  Health checks and testing for blood-borne viruses, including Hepatitis C.
·  Detox help.
·  Medication-assisted treatment and naloxone dispensing.
·  A needle exchange service.
·  Dedicated outreach team to support homeless and rough sleeping clients.
·  Dedicated criminal justice team.
·  Counselling provision.
·  Support from peers who have been through similar experiences.
·  Ongoing recovery support, including SMART recovery groups and Forward Connect meetings.
·  Specialist services to support young people through our partner, Open Road, which is delivered in the community (not the hub).
·  Transitional specialist service for 18–29-year-olds delivered in partnership with Open Road.

 We also deliver a women's only coffee morning for our female clients every Thursday between 10:30am and 12pm.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

We are a user led abstinence based group, which means we agree collectively to reduce, but ultimately stop the use of cannabis, spice and legal highs within our membership.
 
We recognise the damage our drug misuse can do to ourselves and those around us and we choose to seek help from others who have recovered successfully from serious addictions. We have no affiliation to other mutual aid groups such as NA (Narcotics Anonymous) and SMART (Self Management and Recovery Training) but we do support and commend their work. We often refer our members to both meetings and others. We strongly believe that no one system works for everyone and we encourage our members to experience and embrace many different recovery systems, activities and communities.

We are not a cannabis appreciation society and we do not advocate legalisation. We do however acknowledge the particular CBD health benefits and call for greater and more transparent research. Similarly we recognise the failure of subsequent governments to sufficiently support appropriate treatment and recovery programmes.

We have achieved many levels of success within our membership, our groups have produced and maintained many years of clean-time. We have done this by creating a series of local meetings in a safe, confidential, non-judgmental and supportive environment, where members can rebuild their lives together.

ElementText:
Change Grow Live Birmingham is a free and confidential drug and alcohol service for adults. We offer treatment and recovery services to support anyone experiencing difficulties with substance misuse in a range of local community and clinical settings. Our recovery teams include doctors, non-medical prescribers, recovery coordinators, nurses, recovery motivators, service user representatives, and volunteers. We also work with Intuitive Thinking Skills, DATUS, and KIKIT to provide specialist support in our Throughcare offer.

We provide:
·	Confidential advice and information about drugs and alcohol
·	A tailored package of care
·	Healthcare clinics and blood-borne virus testing
·	Residential detoxification and rehabilitation options
·	Ambulatory detox in our hubs
·	Throughcare (group sessions from our recovery motivators and partners)
·	Harm minimisation
·	Needle Exchange and safe storage
·	Shared Care (121 sessions in your local GP surgery)

Depending on your situation, you may be referred to one of our in-house specialist teams. These teams include the Women’s and Families team, Criminal Justice, IPS Employment team, the Veteran’s group, Buvidal team and Homeless & Rough Sleeper team.

Our Prostate Cancer Support Group is a patient-led self-help organisation. The Group comprises of men and their partners who have lived through the trials and tribulations of the prostate cancer journey.

We keep ourselves up to date with the latest medical treatments and research into the disease and with the latest thinking on how nutritional supplements and alternative medicines can help in the fight against the disease.

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

How we can help
We're here for adults in Luton who are struggling with alcohol and/or drug use. We'll listen to your needs and help you set goals so we can tailor your support. We believe everyone has the ability to change, and we're here to help you do it.

Alcohol
People use alcohol for different reasons – to be sociable, to relieve stress, cope with anxiety, and many other reasons. However, your drinking may be affecting you in ways you may not realise. You have the potential to change your drinking. We are here to help you achieve it. 

Drugs
We offer free and confidential advice and information around drugs. Whether you want to reduce your drug use or stop altogether, we're here for you.
We have a needle exchange programme and can offer advice about safer injecting. We also offer free naloxone and training on how to use it.

Contact us
If you'd like to get in touch, the best way would be to give us a call on 0800 054 6603.  You can find out more about what we do and ask any questions you might have. Don't forget to follow us on social media to see what we're up to.

OrganisationName: Cgl - West Kent Drug & Alcohol Wellbeing Service Maidstone
ElementText:
The West Kent Drug & Alcohol Wellbeing Service offers a pathway to recovery for adults who misuse drugs or alcohol. 

The team at CGL will discuss your challenges and goals with you and answer any questions you have. We can help you to find the tools you need to meet your goals, as well as any extra support you need along the way.

The Service offers a range of intensive community-based support, treatment and rehabilitation services that are designed to meet your needs.  The service is free and confidential. It is available to anyone 18 or over who lives in West Kent. It offers:
·  Treatment to help you reduce or stop the harmful use of substances, including (but not limited to) alcohol, heroin, cocaine and cannabis.
·  Personalised support based on your needs and what you'd like to achieve.
·  One-to-one and group sessions.
·  Assessment and treatment provided by an experienced team of health and care staff, nurses and doctors.
·  Access to advice and support from people who share similar life experiences.
·  Reach service for those who require the extra support to access services.
·  Dedicated Criminal Justice team.
·  Needle Exchange access for client using illicit and image performance enhancing drugs.
·  Support with Blood Borne Virus testing (i.e Hepatitis) and immunisation.

OrganisationName: Southend Treatment And Recovery Service (Stars) - The Forward Trust
ElementText:
Southend Treatment and Recovery Service (also known as STARS) is delivered by The Forward Trust alongside partners Open Road. The service helps people aged 18 or over who are experiencing challenges with their use of drugs and/or alcohol or people who are impacted indirectly because a significant other is experiencing these challenges (it doesn’t matter if the significant other is not ready to get support themselves).

Services delivered at our Southend hub include:
·  One-to-one and group support.
·  Health checks and testing for blood-borne viruses, including Hepatitis C.
·  Detox help.
·  Medication-assisted treatment and naloxone dispensing.
·  A needle exchange service.
·  Dedicated outreach team to support homeless and rough sleeping clients.
·  Dedicated criminal justice team.
·  Counselling provision.
·  Support from peers who have been through similar experiences.
·  Ongoing recovery support, including SMART recovery groups and Forward Connect meetings.
·  Specialist services to support young people through our partner, Open Road, which is delivered in the community (not the hub).
·  Transitional specialist service for 18–29-year-olds delivered in partnership with Open Road.

 We also deliver a women's only coffee morning for our female clients every Thursday between 10:30am and 12pm.

OrganisationName: Essex Community Rehabilitation Service – The Forward Trust
ElementText:
The Forward Trust’s Essex service offers dedicated abstinence-based recovery pathways for individuals and families affected by drug and alcohol use, delivered through two SHARP programmes at Wickford and Braintree. These programmes provide structured, therapeutic support that helps people rebuild stability, confidence, and long-term wellbeing.

Alongside abstinence pathways, we offer a suite of specialist interventions designed to meet people wherever they are in their recovery:
·  Brink of Change - a 6-week CBT-based programme consisting of OST-focused sessions and psychoeducational workshops.
·  Non-addiction counselling - emotional and psychological support delivered by trainee counsellors.
·  Addiction counselling - a therapeutic space for individuals ready to explore their relationship with substances.
·  M-PACT - a structured programme supporting families affected by parental substance use.

Together, these services create a flexible, person-centred offer that empowers individuals and families to move forward with clarity, confidence, and the right level of support.

OrganisationName: The Bridges, Hull - The Forward Trust
ElementText:
The Bridges - Hull is a residential rehabilitation in the heart of Hull owned by The Forward Trust. For over 20 years, the service has provided residential care and treatment for people with drug and/or alcohol issues, helping to change the lives of hundreds of individuals.

As a Care Quality Commission (CQC) registered service, the ‘two-stage treatment’ model runs from as short as 12 weeks to as long as 24 weeks. The programme is based on the 12-step model and features a range of individual and group activities, including therapy, counselling, meditation, study groups, and social activities.

Friendly, non-judgemental, professional support is delivered from Forward’s dedicated support team - many with lived experience themselves of addiction and recovery. The research-led treatment approach ensures that The Bridges is able to support every client on their recovery journey - both individually and as a group.

Accommodation at The Bridges - Hull is safe, secure, and ensures privacy when needed. There are also communal spaces for clients to socialise in, such as a TV lounge, fully equipped gym, and a spacious dining room.

How we can help
We're here for adults in Luton who are struggling with alcohol and/or drug use. We'll listen to your needs and help you set goals so we can tailor your support. We believe everyone has the ability to change, and we're here to help you do it.

Alcohol
People use alcohol for different reasons – to be sociable, to relieve stress, cope with anxiety, and many other reasons. However, your drinking may be affecting you in ways you may not realise. You have the potential to change your drinking. We are here to help you achieve it. 

Drugs
We offer free and confidential advice and information around drugs. Whether you want to reduce your drug use or stop altogether, we're here for you.
We have a needle exchange programme and can offer advice about safer injecting. We also offer free naloxone and training on how to use it.

Contact us
If you'd like to get in touch, the best way would be to give us a call on 0800 054 6603.  You can find out more about what we do and ask any questions you might have. Don't forget to follow us on social media to see what we're up to.

OrganisationName: Change Grow Live Drug And Alcohol Service – Manchester
ElementText:
Change Grow Live Manchester work with anyone looking to make positive changes related to drug & alcohol use. We approach treatment with an open mind, free from judgement. If your goals don't include treatment and recovery, but you do want to reduce the harmful impacts of drug & alcohol use, we can help with this too.  

Change Grow Live are a national organisation, with the aim to help people change the direction of their lives, grow as individuals and live life to its full potential. In Manchester, we offer support with harm reduction, needle exchange, housing, criminal justice, employment, education & training and homeless outreach. We have links with other services, including a smoking addiction service also under the Change Grow Live umbrella, called Be Smoke Free, and we offer a service which works specifically with young people, called Eclypse. We work with Emerging Futures and Acorn to deliver our psychosocial intervention groups and after-treatment care, and LGBT Foundation to provide specialist support related to LGBTQ+ issues for those in treatment. 

Change Grow Live's teams work in partnership with service users to assess their requirements and to plan individual treatment plans and support that will help service users to address their problems and achieve their personal goals.

We provide a full range of treatment and recovery interventions for people who require services for their drug or alcohol use. We do this by providing:

- Initial assessment to work out what support will benefit you
- Brief interventions (including harm reduction advice and support over the phone)
- Medically assisted treatment (MAT)
- Support sessions with recovery coordinators and engagement workers – one-to-one and in small groups
- Second opinions when requested by a GP
- Community detox
- Referral for in-patient detox
- Links to rehab clinics
- Peer Support groups – informal drop-ins, and structured group programmes
- Health assessments
- Blood-borne virus (BBV) tests and treatment - HIV, Hep B and Hep C
- Hep B vaccinations
- Needle Syringe Programmes (AKA needle exchange)


We also deliver free online training to professionals on topics related to drug & alcohol use, which you can find on our Eventbrite page:  https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/cc/adult-drug-alcohol-training-for-professionals-2132019

The Royal College of Podiatry is the professional body for podiatrists in the UK, setting academic and clinical standards, promoting research and education, and raising awareness of foot health. 
Podiatrists are regulated professionals who are experts in assessing, diagnosing, and treating conditions, injuries, diseases, and traumas of the foot and lower limb. They prevent, manage, and correct foot irregularities, relieve pain, treat infection, and keep people of all ages mobile and active. 
Podiatrists (also known as chiropodists) are regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) and work across both the NHS and independent/private sectors.
While certain NHS treatments are fully funded based on specific local medical criteria, independent and private podiatry services are typically fee-paying unless otherwise specified.
Throughout their careers, the College supports podiatrists to deliver high-quality foot and lower-limb care and to continue developing their skills.

ElementText:
The Bridges - Hull is a residential rehabilitation in the heart of Hull owned by The Forward Trust. For over 20 years, the service has provided residential care and treatment for people with drug and/or alcohol issues, helping to change the lives of hundreds of individuals.

As a Care Quality Commission (CQC) registered service, the ‘two-stage treatment’ model runs from as short as 12 weeks to as long as 24 weeks. The research-led treatment approach ensures that The Bridges is able to support every client on their recovery journey - both individually and as a group.

Accommodation at The Bridges - Hull is safe, secure, and ensures privacy when needed. There are also communal spaces for clients to socialise in, such as a TV lounge, fully equipped gym, and a spacious dining room.
